content.title: About
content.content: Rice noodles are thin strands made from rice flour, typically gluten‑free. When cooked they become soft, slightly chewy and translucent. They are a staple in many Asian cuisines, especially Thai, Vietnamese and Chinese dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice noodles originated in Southeast Asia, where rice is the dominant crop.
Unlike wheat noodles, they contain virtually no gluten, making them popular among people with celiac disease.
Various shapes exist: wide (similar to fettuccine), thin (vermicelli) and round (spaghetti‑like).
To speed up preparation, the noodles are often pre‑dried and sometimes lightly toasted.
In Japan a similar product made from rice flour is called "soba" (without eggs).

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Rice noodles contain almost no fat, which makes them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Rich source of carbohydrates
items.content: They provide complex carbs that release energy slowly.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Ideal for individuals with gluten intolerance or celiac disease.

items.title: Contains small amounts of B‑vitamins
items.content: Especially thiamine (B1) and niacin (B3), important for metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The soft texture after cooking is gentle on the stomach.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice noodles can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Low in protein and fiber
items.content: Compared with whole‑grain alternatives, they provide limited protein and dietary fiber.

items.title: Sodium in ready‑made dishes
items.content: When paired with pre‑made sauces, the dish can become high in sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boil the noodles in water for 3‑5 minutes until tender, then rinse with cold water to stop cooking. Add them to soups, stir‑fries, salads, or use as a base for cold Asian dishes with a flavorful sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry rice noodles in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked noodles should be eaten within 2‑3 days and stored in the refrigerator in a sealed container.
